title: Field Measurement and Emission Quantification of Volatile Organic Compounds at a Crude Oil Storage Depot
content: Crude oil storage depots are important sources of atmospheric volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, contributing to air pollution and associated environmental concerns. In this study, VOC emissions from storage tanks at a typical crude oil depot were measured through field investigations, and emission rates were quantified at both the component and facility levels. The total VOC emissions were estimated based on field measurements, and the corresponding emission intensity was further evaluated. The results revealed substantial variations in component-level emission rates, with guide pillars exhibiting higher emission rates than breathing valves and support pillars. At the facility level, VOC emission rates ranged from 0.07 to 30.10 L/min, with guide pillars accounting for more than 44% of the total VOC emission rate associated with external floating-roof tanks. The total VOC emissions from the investigated crude oil depot were estimated at 422.24 tonnes, which was lower than the value obtained using engineering estimation methods. Furthermore, the population-averaged VOC emission intensity for typical crude oil depots in China was estimated to be 0.0076%. These findings provide field-based evidence of VOC emission characteristics at both the component and facility levels and highlight the importance of component-specific measurements for improving emission inventories and developing targeted emission-control strategies for crude oil storage depots.
